title: Harmonize SDK transport defaults: keep-alive, pooling, and timeout heuristics
creator: Jordan Kim
description:
Background: SDKs across Python/TypeScript/Go currently have divergent transport defaults (timeouts, connection pooling, keep-alive, and retry heuristics). This causes inconsistent production characteristics for identical workloads when customers switch SDKs or when server-side routing falls back between deployments. Goal: establish a small, well-documented set of cross-SDK transport defaults and feature gates that provide predictable latency and resource usage while preserving streaming ergonomics and safe retry behavior.

Scope and acceptance criteria:
- Define three timeout buckets: connect timeout, socket/read timeout, and total/request timeout. Defaults should be conservative and documented per-language.
- Enable persistent connections/keep-alive by default with platform-appropriate pooling settings. Provide clear knobs to tune per-app.
- Ensure streaming responses (server-sent tokens / chunked) are not interrupted by intermediate read timeout unless explicitly configured.
- Define retry semantics for idempotent operations (embeddings, stateless generation with deterministic bodies) and when not to retry (streaming, non-idempotent function-calling).
- Implement a unified transport config/constructor in each SDK that accepts explicit options, environment variables (REDWOOD_SDK_*), and falls back to sensible defaults.
- Provide code examples for each language showing how to tune keep-alive, max connections, and timeouts for low-latency and high-throughput workloads.
- Add unit and integration tests that validate pooled connection reuse and streaming resilience under timeouts.

Proposed per-language default recommendations (initial proposal):
- Node (TypeScript/JS): use an http(s).Agent with keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 64, keepAliveMsecs: 5000. Default connectTimeout=2000ms, socketTimeout=120000ms, totalTimeout=300000ms. Expose agent options via SDK client constructor and REDWOOD_SDK_NODE_AGENT_OPTIONS env var (JSON).
- Python: use a single requests.Session or httpx.Client (sync/async) with urllib3 PoolManager: pool_maxsize=50, maxsize per host=50, block=False. Default connect_timeout=2s, read_timeout=120s, total_timeout=300s. Streaming clients should use read_timeout=None to avoid truncating token streams unless user overrides. Expose REDWOOD_SDK_PY_TIMEOUTS and REDWOOD_SDK_PY_POOL env variables.
- Go: configure http.Transport with IdleConnTimeout=90s, MaxIdleConns=200, MaxIdleConnsPerHost=100, TLSHandshakeTimeout=2s. Default Dialer timeout 2s, ResponseHeaderTimeout 30s, overall request context for total timeout 300s. Provide a Builder that takes a TransportOptions struct and env-driven defaults REDWOOD_SDK_GO_*.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Keep-alive default reduces latency for bursty workloads at the cost of holding idle connections. Conservative pool sizes chosen to balance file descriptor usage in server-hosted contexts.
- Longer read/streaming timeouts prevent spurious stream terminations; but we keep a shorter ResponseHeaderTimeout in Go to fail fast on slow handshakes.
- Retries are enabled by default only for idempotent endpoints with exponential backoff capped at 3 attempts; streaming endpoints never auto-retry.

Migration plan and rollout:
1) Land cross-SDK config primitives and env var parsing (this ticket).
2) Add defaults and test harnesses; create e2e tests simulating connection churn and streaming under delays.
3) Soft-launch by adding deprecation warnings when user overrides absent; document recommended settings in SDK migration guide.
4) Roll default change behind a feature flag for 2 weeks to collect telemetry (latency, connection reuse, error rates).

Deliverables:
- SDK client constructors that accept TransportOptions / AgentOptions / TransportConfig.
- Language-specific docs and examples (README snippets).
- Integration tests and perf benchmarks (simple harness that measures cold vs warm request latency and token-throughput with pooling enabled).

References and artifacts:
- Design notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/transport-sdk-defaults (internal)
- Initial perf microbench PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2073
- Incident investigation: CON-2024-11-14-conn-thundering documented link: https://drive.redwood/investigations/CON-2024-11

Open questions:
- Exact default pool sizes for small-hosted vs large-enterprise Dedicated deployments (should we detect cgroup limits?).
- Should streaming read timeouts default to infinite or a very large value? Proposed: infinite for streaming clients, finite for request/response flows.
- Env var naming and serialization format (JSON vs comma-separated key=val).
